repinRationale.why: THE FROZEN v4 BUNDLE BUYS EQUIPMENT THE GAME REFUSES TO SELL, AND PRICES A NON-CRIT AT 1/2.5. v4 is pinned at 2026-07-14, which predates the entire 2026-07-28 exhaustive logic review; the remediation campaign then closed 115 issues across nine sessions (128 filed — remediation found 26 of its own), 41 of them in modules the L0 differential watches (39 at plan time plus #169/#170, re-milestoned out of Track A once they turned out to move three fixtures). Sessions 7-9 deliberately COLLECTED their reds instead of absorbing them one at a time, so this is ONE re-pin for the whole campaign — bought at the price of a red Pages deploy from S8 until now, a trade taken knowingly and recorded on main in 13274fe3. 14 of 21 fixtures diverge against v4; all 14 are attributed below to a named commit, and the other 7 reproduce BYTE-IDENTICALLY.
repinRationale.countByEventNotByIndex: Every number here is an LCS event count (`node scripts/sim/event-diff.mjs <before-dir> [after-dir]`, keyed on fn+args, NOT on tick), because the positional `diffTraces` count that baseline-zero prints inflates badly: 12-warp-u1 reads 1991 positional divergences and is 697 event edits; 08-starved-u1.1 reads 1742 and is 704. The #69 entry below had to hand-count this; the tool is committed now so the ledger is re-derivable rather than retyped.

fourRootCauses.#203 + #220: mostEfficientEquipment ranked LOCKED slots and the always-level-2 block bought them unguarded. The v4 oracle records buyEquipment("Arbalest") and buyEquipment("Gambeson") on a save that has neither unlocked, then stalls at tick 2 and buys nothing for the rest of the run (15 events total). The fixed build buys Dagger/Boots and keeps going: 162 events. THAT ORACLE TRACE WAS ALWAYS WRONG — re-pinning it is the correction, not a laundering.
fourRootCauses.#169 + #170: gammaBurstPct's off sentinel was 1 rather than 0, and survived a heirloom swap down. Labelled sim-blind by the campaign's own partition and it moves three fixtures — the label was derived from 'does this module terminate in a wrapped mutator', which is the wrong question for a module that only computes an ESTIMATE that calc.ts reads and stance.ts turns into setFormation.
fourRootCauses.#290 + #294: calc.ts treated formation 5 (uber-Wind) as a halving formation at four sites. #290 named two; the mechanical scan its own scoping claim implied found four.
fourRootCauses.#199 + #212 + #295: a non-crit was priced at getMegaCritDamageMult(0) = 1/critD instead of 1. On a zero-crit save — which is the whole shallow corpus, measured critD = 2 — AT understated its own damage by 2.5x, and every gear/stance/farm decision downstream of calcHDratio() inherited it. Clearest single reading: on 08-starved-u1 setFormation("0")/setFormation(3) become setFormation(2) from tick 71, i.e. AT stops cowering in X/Barrier and takes Dominance because it has stopped believing it is 2.5x weaker than it is.

repinRationale.fourControls:
Four negative controls, each a number rather than an argument:
  1. THE BUNDLE IS THE SAME BUNDLE. `cmp dist/autotrimps.user.js tests/fixtures/oracle/autotrimps.oracle.user.js` exits 0 — the frozen v5 oracle is byte-identical to the working build, so every move above is oracle-vs-oracle behaviour with zero harness, bundler or runtime drift mixed in. The runtime fingerprint is unchanged too (node v26.0.0 / jsdom 29.1.1 / clone 5.10.1 / darwin arm64).
  2. SEVEN FIXTURES REPRODUCE BYTE-IDENTICALLY — exactly the seven baseline-zero was GREEN on against v4 immediately before the re-record: 02-mid-u1 x3, 04-u2-radon, 05-maps-u1, 09-housing-u2, 11-portal-u1. Where the campaign should be inert it IS inert. This is the check the #105 entry demands be repeated on any future re-pin.
  3. 12-warp-u1 IS INERT ACROSS THE FORMATION COMMIT (step C), byte-identical at 2011 events. Formation 5 is uber-Wind, which that fixture never reaches, so a formation-5 mirror correction SHOULD be invisible there — and is. Predicted before it was measured.
  4. EVERYTHING AFTER 2cfef274 MOVES NOTHING. All 21 fixtures at step D are byte-identical to the final recording — so the rest of S9 Wave 1 (#198/#244/#296, #233/#250, #229-#231, #248/#249), Wave 2 (maps), and Waves 3-5 (24 more issues) contribute ZERO trace movement. That reproduces, in one measurement, the per-wave "moves NO traces" results S9 recorded separately.
repinRationale.andItInvertsTheCensus: Same warning as #105: the blind-spot census counts divergences of a MUTATED build against the committed traces, so against a stale oracle it INVERTS — restoring a bug makes the mutant agree (reported BLIND) while the clean build is the one that diverges. Between S8 and this re-pin the census was therefore meaningless on 14 of 21 fixtures. A census number means nothing unless baseline-zero reads zero, so the census was re-run AFTER this re-pin, not before, and tests/sim/blind-spot-census.md is the post-re-pin table.
repinRationale.proofItLaundersNothing: Controls 1 and 2 above are the laundering check, and control 4 is the scope check. Stated as a rule for the next re-pin: (a) prove the oracle bundle equals the build you are recording with, (b) prove every fixture the old oracle already agreed with reproduces BYTE-IDENTICALLY, (c) attribute every remaining fixture to a named commit measured on its own, and (d) show that the commits you did NOT name move nothing. Re-record to absorb a reviewed, root-caused, intentional behaviour change — never to make a red go away.
repinRationale.howToReDerive:
node scripts/sim/build-oracle.mjs   # rebuild the frozen bundle from the tag
node scripts/sim/record-oracle.mjs  # re-record the 21 traces
node scripts/sim/event-diff.mjs <dir-of-pre-fix-traces> [tests/fixtures/traces]
The pre-fix traces are the committed ones at tag baseline/pre-s7 (01836cb7) — unchanged from #196 through S9, verified with `git diff baseline/pre-s7 HEAD -- tests/fixtures/traces/` returning empty.
repinRationale.portabilityCheck: The traces were recorded on darwin/arm64 (see the runtime block below) and the GitHub Actions CI gate — linux/x64 — passes on them: runs 30515476052 and 30515621115, both SUCCESS, 2056/2056 tests, 0 skipped. (Those runs were against the unsquashed S10 branch, preserved at tag `s10-chain`; `main` carries the squash.) That matters because this repo treats trace portability as PROVEN and therefore reads any CI-only divergence as a REAL regression rather than an environmental one. A fresh re-record that reproduced only on the recording machine would break that rule silently, so the cross-platform green is part of the evidence, not a formality.

v4RepinRationale.why: THE FROZEN ORACLE CARRIED THE VERY BUGS THE NEW FIXTURES EXIST TO CATCH. v3 is pinned at 2026-07-12; #93 (mostEfficientHousing's divisor), #96 and #101 (Rhypo's bonfire clause) all shipped AFTER it. So the v3 bundle contained, verbatim, `let housingBonus = game.buildings.Hut.increase.by` (#93's bug) and `bonfire > getPageSetting2("Rhypofarmstack").slice(-1)` (#101's). Nobody noticed because THE CORPUS NEVER REACHED EITHER REGION — which is precisely what the blind-spot census measured (both rows BLIND, 0/17). The stale oracle and the blind spots were the SAME phenomenon, and adding the coverage is what exposed it.
v4RepinRationale.andItInvertsTheCensus: The census counts divergences of a MUTATED build against the committed oracle traces. Against a v3 oracle, restoring #93's bug makes the mutated build AGREE with the oracle — zero divergences, reported as BLIND — while the CLEAN build is the one that diverges. A census number only means anything when baseline-zero is zero, so the re-pin is a precondition for the fixtures, not a side effect of them.
v4RepinRationale.proofItLaundersNothing: baseline-zero was GREEN against v3 immediately before the re-pin: current src and the v3 bundle produce identical traces across the whole existing corpus. So re-recording 01-08 against v4 must reproduce them BYTE-IDENTICALLY — and it does, 17/17 cmp-clean, verified twice (once bare, once after the new fixtures landed). The re-pin therefore changes behavior ONLY in the regions the old corpus could not see, where v3 was carrying the predecessors of known, reviewed, shipped fixes. REPEAT THIS CHECK ON ANY FUTURE RE-PIN — it is what separates a re-pin from a laundered regression.

supersededRecordAdditive196.kind: ADDITIVE RE-RECORD — the oracle bundle did NOT change (still oracle/v4-post-fix-sweep) and neither did src/. This is not a re-pin. One more native mutator is now WATCHED; nothing observed before is observed differently.
supersededRecordAdditive196.what: scripts/sim/recorder.mjs adds `setGather` to MUTATORS, plus a new DEDUPE_ON_CHANGE set that records a mutator only when its args differ from the previous RECORDED call. gather.ts (384 lines) had no native-mutator terminus at all, so baseline-zero and the blind-spot census were structurally unable to see it — a green suite was never evidence about the gather decision. It needed no new fixture: AT already calls setGather on 100% of the corpus.
supersededRecordAdditive196.whyDedupe: AT re-asserts the gather target EVERY TICK — measured 1500/1500 on every fixture — across only two or three distinct values (trimps / buildings / metal). Recording call-for-call would have added ~31,500 rows of pure re-assertion corpus-wide and drowned the signal; the decision AT actually makes is the TRANSITION SEQUENCE, measured at 10-225 per run. DEDUPE_ON_CHANGE is deliberately a narrow, declared exception: every other mutator is still recorded call-for-call, because for the buy mutators repetition IS information (buying the same building twice is not the same as once). The dedup gates only the trace.push — orig.apply runs unconditionally, so game behaviour is untouched, and the key compares against the last RECORDED value, so genuine A->B->A oscillation is still captured in full.
supersededRecordAdditive196.proofItLaundersNothing: +660 setGather rows across all 21 traces, and EVERY NON-setGather ROW IS BYTE-IDENTICAL — verified programmatically by stripping setGather events from both the committed predecessor and the new file and comparing the remainder (21/21 identical). baseline-zero then passes 21/21 against the new traces. That byte-identity is the check this file demands on any re-record, and it is what separates widening the observation lens from laundering a behaviour change.
supersededRecordAdditive196.sensitivityCheck: REACH != SENSITIVITY, and the first attempt FAILED this check — usefully. The census probe was originally injected into autogather3(), came back BLIND on all 21 runs, and was right to: ManualGather2 defaults to 1 (settings-defs.ts:51), which routes to manualLabor2() — where all twelve setGather decisions live — while autogather3() only runs at value 2, which no fixture uses. The mutation landed and the bundle changed, and it still measured nothing. Retargeted at manualLabor2: SEEN, 14,661 divergences on 18/21 runs. If a future corpus change makes that row go BLIND, the net has lost its ability to see gather regressions — fix the corpus, not the row.
supersededRecordAdditive196.whatIsStillBlind: Four other unwrapped natives remain invisible BY CORPUS DEPTH, not by harness bug (#196): selectHeirloom/equipHeirloom (every fixture holds ZERO heirlooms), changeGeneratorState and naturePurchase (z230+; deepest fixture is z62), and the autoBattle.* methods (unlocked on no fixture). All five resolve as functions on window after bootGame, so the recorder could wrap them the moment a deep enough save exists.

supersededRecord.kind: HARNESS RE-RECORD — the oracle bundle did NOT change, and neither did src/. This is not a re-pin. The SIMULATED GAME changed: it now runs its own trigger system, which it never had.
supersededRecord.what: scripts/sim/driver.mjs tickOnce() now calls checkTriggers() after gameLoop(). boot.mjs stubs `window.setTimeout = () => 0` to suppress the game's self-driving loops, and the game calls checkTriggers() during play from exactly ONE place — costUpdatesTimeout(), a `setTimeout(costUpdatesTimeout, 250)` loop (main.js:17970). So it NEVER FIRED. Forge is a *trigger*, not an upgrade (config.js:13226, fires at >=350 metal): Forge never unlocked -> metal.max pinned at 500 on every save in the corpus -> Coordination (507 metal at done=2) permanently unaffordable. AutoTrimps bought Coordination ZERO times in the entire history of the proof net, and the deep fixtures ran metal-capped (owned === max === 500) on up to 100% of their ticks.
supersededRecord.why: Every metal, gear, storage and housing conclusion the sim ever produced was measured against a DEAD economy — which is how #57 came to be designed against a premise ('Coordination gets starved by lesser spending') that was structurally unobservable in the simulator. This is #66 in a new costume: a stubbed environment silently disabling a whole game subsystem while every gate stayed green. Of costUpdatesTimeout's five calls only checkTriggers has game-state effect here — the four checkButtons() calls resolve to DOM class swaps (updateButtonColor) plus updateSRBuyAmt, which no-ops while usingScreenReader is false (boot sets it) — so cherry-picking it is shown, not assumed. Cadence is exact, not approximate: resources only move inside gameLoop, so a trigger can only become newly-affordable immediately after one.
supersededRecord.honesty: THIS RE-RECORD IS NOT ADDITIVE, and unlike #90/#98 it cannot claim byte-identity. Counted BY EVENT (LCS over fn+args, not by index): 04-u2-radon reproduces BYTE-IDENTICAL (1204 -> 1204, 0 inserted / 0 deleted) — U2's economy is radon-based and never touches Forge, which is the control proving the change is inert where it should be. The shallow U1 saves move a little and entirely explicably (01-early: 33 -> 33, +buyBuilding(Forge), +buyUpgrade(Efficiency); 03-challenge: 30 -> 30, +Forge). The deep saves genuinely RESHAPE (06-deep: 1765 -> 2013 events, 303 inserted / 55 deleted; 08-starved: 1601 -> 1872, 649 in / 378 out), dominated by setFormation churn — the bot now has metal, buys more gear, and crosses its damage/health thresholds on different ticks. That is the intended consequence of a working economy, not drift, but it is a real trajectory change and is recorded here as one.
supersededRecord.sensitivityCheck: REACH != SENSITIVITY (#98). 08-starved-u1 earns its place by leaving AT's damage threshold UNSATURATED, and a live economy buys more gear there (equipment levels 70 -> 79), which could in principle saturate it and quietly blunt the net. Re-verified after this re-record: tests/sim/damage-sensitivity.test.ts's POSITIVE control (1,000,000x damage injection) still goes RED against the fresh traces. If a future corpus change makes that control pass, the net has lost its ability to see combat regressions — fix the corpus, not the test.

supersededRecord2.kind: ADDITIVE RE-RECORD — the oracle bundle did NOT change. This is not a re-pin.
supersededRecord2.what: Added four corpus saves (05-maps-u1, 06-deep-u1, 07-map-cap-u1, 08-starved-u1) and two recorded mutators (buyMap, recycleBelow). Traces for the new saves were recorded fresh; traces for 01-04 were re-recorded and verified BYTE-IDENTICAL to their committed predecessors (all 10 files, cmp-clean). That byte-identity is the proof this was additive and not a laundered behavior change — it is the check to repeat on any future corpus growth.
supersededRecord2.why: The net was structurally blind to the bot. It recorded only buy events, and every save decoded to world=4 with mapsUnlocked=false, so maps.ts:253 short-circuited calcOurDmg out of every decision: a 1,000,000x damage multiplier passed the whole sim suite GREEN (#98). Two DISTINCT fixes were needed, and the second is the one that is easy to miss. (1) REACH: the recorder was watching the wrong functions — AT creates maps via buyMap() (38 callsites) and mass-recycles via recycleBelow() (3), neither of which was wrapped, while the wrapped recycleMap is only the 100-map-cap fallback. Plus the corpus could not reach maps at all. (2) SATURATION: reach alone did NOT restore sensitivity. On 06 (deep, mapping, formations, calcOurDmg called every tick) the 1e6x injection STILL diffed to ZERO, because AT's damage decisions are threshold predicates — enoughDamage = (dmg * cutoff > enemyHealth) — and on 06 that predicate is already TRUE, so a buff cannot move it. 08-starved-u1 is damage-starved but perked, leaving the threshold UNSATURATED; the same injection now yields 1542 divergences there. Calling a function is not the same as depending on its answer. tests/sim/damage-sensitivity.test.ts makes this a permanent, self-checking mutation gate.

oracle.why: TWO reasons, both load-bearing. (1) HARNESS WAS BLIND: until #66, scripts/sim/boot.mjs left `usingRealTimeOffline` stuck true after load() — the game's offline-progress replay sets it (main.js:2901) and normally clears it via a setTimeout loop the sim stubs out. AT's mainLoop gates `setScienceNeeded()` + `autoLevelEquipment()` on `!usingRealTimeOffline`, so EVERY trace recorded against phase1-faithful was recorded with all gear-buying and science tracking disabled: zero buyEquipment events, U1 buyBuilding nearly absent. The L0 net was comparing a crippled AT against a crippled AT. (2) THE OLD ORACLE ENSHRINED A SHIPPED BUG: phase1-faithful contains #63 (needGymystic hardcoded true → scienceNeeded permanently +5,000,000). On 02-mid-u1 the old oracle computes scienceNeeded=5,001,452 and gathers science where the fixed build computes 1,452 and gathers buildings; every downstream buy timing cascades from that one number. The (save,index,fn) waiver mechanism is built for a few LOCALIZED fix divergences, not a wholly shifted trajectory (~130 brittle entries). Re-pinning was the correct move, and the v2 traces are strictly RICHER than the old ones (they contain the buyEquipment/buyBuilding events the old ones structurally could not), so the net is more sensitive after the re-pin than before it. NOTE: re-pinning is NOT routine — a naked oracle change is exactly the accidental-drift alarm this net exists to raise. Only re-pin behind a root-caused, reviewed, intentional behavior change.

notes.coverage: radon-only; the U1 corpus (01/02/03) never reaches RbuyJobs. The 04-u2-radon save (added #47) DOES run RbuyJobs — yet it produces ZERO L0 delta for THIS fixture's numeric window (verified 2026-07-10): L0 records buyJob(name, buyMax, force), and for a normal buy the fix only shifts the worker QUANTITY computed internally, not buyJob's args (buyMax=true carries no count). NOTE this is empirical, NOT a structural invariant: freeWorkers (jobs.ts:492) also feeds an `if (freeWorkers<=0) return` gate BEFORE any buyJob call, so a different U2 save/seed whose fixed-vs-buggy freeWorkers straddles 0 WOULD surface a real L0 divergence (missing buyJob calls that tick). For 04-u2-radon it stays well above the gate, so the fix remains gated by the jobs.RbuyJobs L1 regression (156→33), not an L0 waiver. This corrects the earlier prediction that adding a U2 save would force an L0 waiver here.
